properties.name: debug
properties.description: Any value but `false` (for example `--debug`) logs the condition evaluation report: which auto-configured beans were created, and why the others were not.

properties.name: spring.application.json
properties.description: Properties as one JSON object (see `SPRING_APPLICATION_JSON`).

properties.name: spring.application.name
properties.description: The application's name: the context's id, and the name in the startup lines (`application` when not set).

properties.name: spring.autoconfigure.exclude
properties.description: The auto-configurations to leave out, by class or module name.

properties.name: spring.banner.location
properties.description: The banner file. `${spring-boot.version}`, `${spring-boot.formatted-version}` and other `${...}` in it are replaced.

properties.name: spring.devtools.restart.enabled
properties.description: Whether a hot reload restarts the context when the generated code changed.

properties.name: spring.json.datatype.datetime.read-date-timestamps-as-nanoseconds
properties.description: Reads timestamps with a fraction. Default: the value of `spring.json.deserialization.read-date-timestamps-as-nanoseconds`.

properties.name: spring.json.datatype.datetime.write-date-timestamps-as-nanoseconds
properties.description: Timestamps with a fraction. Default: the value of `spring.json.serialization.write-date-timestamps-as-nanoseconds`.

properties.name: spring.json.datatype.datetime.write-dates-as-timestamps
properties.description: Dates as numbers. Default: the value of `spring.json.serialization.write-dates-as-timestamps`.

properties.name: spring.json.datatype.datetime.write-durations-as-timestamps
properties.description: Durations as numbers. Default: the value of `spring.json.serialization.write-durations-as-timestamps`.

properties.name: spring.json.default-property-inclusion
properties.description: Which properties are written.

properties.name: spring.json.deserialization.accept-float-as-int
properties.description: `1.0` can be read into an `int`.

properties.name: spring.json.deserialization.fail-on-null-for-primitives
properties.description: `null` for a non-nullable number or `bool` fails the read.

properties.name: spring.json.deserialization.fail-on-unknown-properties
properties.description: An unknown JSON property fails the read.

properties.name: spring.json.deserialization.read-date-timestamps-as-nanoseconds
properties.description: Reads timestamps with a fraction.

properties.name: spring.json.mapper.default-view-inclusion
properties.description: Properties without `@JsonView` appear in every view.

properties.name: spring.json.mapper.sort-properties-alphabetically
properties.description: Writes properties in alphabetical order.

properties.name: spring.json.property-naming-strategy
properties.description: How field names become JSON names.

properties.name: spring.json.schemas-registry.properties
properties.description: The schemas of `spring.json.schemas` and of `@JsonSchemaSource` go into the registry bean, the app's own too.

properties.name: spring.json.schemas[*].location
properties.description: Where it is: `resources:schemas/order.json`, an `https://` address or `github:owner/repo/path@ref`; the build downloads a remote one.

properties.name: spring.json.schemas[*].name
properties.description: The name of its root class, instead of its `title`.

properties.name: spring.json.schemas[*].prefix
properties.description: What the names of its classes start with (`Api`: `ApiOrder`).

properties.name: spring.json.schemas[*].sha256
properties.description: The SHA-256 of a remote schema (hex): the build refuses another.

properties.name: spring.json.serialization.indent-output
properties.description: Pretty-printed JSON.

properties.name: spring.json.serialization.write-date-timestamps-as-nanoseconds
properties.description: Timestamps with a fraction.

properties.name: spring.json.serialization.write-dates-as-timestamps
properties.description: Dates as numbers. `spring.json.datatype.datetime.write-dates-as-timestamps` does the same and wins.

properties.name: spring.json.serialization.write-durations-as-timestamps
properties.description: Durations as numbers.

properties.name: spring.json.time-zone
properties.description: `UTC`, `Z` or a fixed offset (`+02:00`); named zones such as `Europe/Berlin` fail, as Dart has no time zone database.

properties.name: spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase
properties.description: How long the context waits for the beans of one shutdown phase to stop.

properties.name: spring.main.allow-bean-definition-overriding
properties.description: A second bean with the same name replaces the first instead of failing the start.

properties.name: spring.main.banner-mode
properties.description: Where the banner is printed. `false` is the same as `off`.

properties.name: spring.main.lazy-initialization
properties.description: Creates every bean on first use instead of at the start: a faster start, but a broken bean fails later.

properties.name: spring.main.log-startup-info
properties.description: Logs the "Starting …", active profiles and "Started … in N seconds" lines.

properties.name: spring.main.register-shutdown-hook
properties.description: Closes the context on SIGINT or SIGTERM, so `@PreDestroy` methods run (VM only). Off by default, unlike in Spring Boot.

properties.name: spring.messages.always-use-message-format
properties.description: Formats messages without arguments too, so `''` becomes `'`.

properties.name: spring.messages.basename
properties.description: The base names of the files. `i18n/errors` (or `i18n.errors`) reads `i18n/errors_{locale}.properties`.

properties.name: spring.messages.cache-duration
properties.description: How long a loaded file is kept before it is read again. Default: kept forever. A number without a unit is in seconds.

properties.name: spring.messages.common-messages
properties.description: Texts shared by every locale; a later file wins.

properties.name: spring.messages.default-locale
properties.description: A locale tried before the system's (not in Spring Boot).

properties.name: spring.messages.encoding
properties.description: The files' encoding; an unknown one fails the start. Default: UTF-8.

properties.name: spring.messages.fallback-to-system-locale
properties.description: Tries the system's locale before the file without a locale.

properties.name: spring.messages.use-code-as-default-message
properties.description: A missing key returns the key itself instead of failing.

properties.name: spring.observations.annotations.enabled
properties.description: Whether `@Observed` works: with `true` the build has the advisor that puts it into effect and writes a proxy for each bean marked `@Observed`; without it, no proxy at all. Read by the generator.

properties.name: spring.resources.embed.exclude
properties.description: Globs below `lib/resources/` (`content/**`) the build does not embed: a Flutter app reads them as its Flutter assets under the same `resources:` locations (the web downloads one when it is read). The configuration (`application*`, `*.properties`, `config/`) is always embedded. Read by the generator.

properties.name: spring.resources.prefetch.delay
properties.description: How long after the app is shown (`stage: app`), so the files of the page shown come first.

properties.name: spring.resources.prefetch.locations
properties.description: Globs below `lib/resources/` (`content/**`) of the text files to put in the file. Empty: none is written. Read by the generator.

properties.name: spring.resources.prefetch.stage
properties.description: When the app downloads it.

properties.name: spring.task.execution.isolates.allow-core-timeout
properties.description: Whether the first `core-size` isolates are stopped when idle too.

properties.name: spring.task.execution.isolates.core-size
properties.description: The isolates started before tasks wait in the queue; not set: one less than the machine has processors (at least one).

properties.name: spring.task.execution.isolates.keep-alive
properties.description: How long an idle isolate stays before it is stopped.

properties.name: spring.task.execution.isolates.max-size
properties.description: The most isolates, reached only when the queue is full; not set: as many as `core-size`.

properties.name: spring.task.execution.isolates.name-prefix
properties.description: The isolates' names in the logs, a number added: `task-1`; in an isolate of the web server's pool, after its name: `isolate-2-task-1`.

properties.name: spring.task.execution.isolates.queue-capacity
properties.description: How many tasks may wait for an isolate; not set: any number, so the pool never grows past `core-size`.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.client-address-header
properties.description: The header a trusted proxy puts the client's address in: `X-Forwarded-For` (a list, read from the right), or a header with one address such as `CF-Connecting-IP`.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.enabled
properties.description: Whether requests are limited. Not set: on when [rules] has a rule, else off; an application that only uses `@RateLimiter` on its controllers sets it to `true` (the start fails when it does not). `false` turns the rules and the annotations off.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.hash-addresses
properties.description: Whether keys made of an address are stored as their HMAC-SHA-256 under [hashSecret], so that the store holds no address in clear.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.hash-secret
properties.description: The secret of [hashAddresses]; required with it. Every server that shares a store needs the same.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.headers
properties.description: Whether the answers carry `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` (of the rule that leaves the least).

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.ipv6-prefix-length
properties.description: How many bits of an IPv6 address say who a client is, 1 to 128: a client is counted by that prefix of its address, the rest zeroed. 64 (the default) is the network a provider gives one client, who chooses the other 64 bits and may change them for every request; 128 counts every address by itself. IPv4 addresses are counted whole, and the trusted proxies are compared by their whole address.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.memory.max-entries
properties.description: The most keys the stores in memory (`memory`, `primary-isolate`) keep; past it the buckets that are full again go, then the keys not used for the longest.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.on-store-failure
properties.description: What happens to a request when the store cannot be reached; a rule may say otherwise for itself.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.rules[*].burst
properties.description: The most requests at once (the size of the bucket) when it is not the count of [limit].

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.rules[*].key
properties.description: Who a bucket belongs to: `user` (the authenticated user, else the client's address; the default), `ip` (the client's address, decided before any authentication work), or a SpEL expression in `#{...}` over `request`, `headers`, `principal`, `authentication`, `address`, `method` and `path` (`#{request.headers['X-Api-Key']}`, header names in any case); an expression that gives nothing counts by address. One that cannot be parsed fails the start; one that names what does not exist counts by address too, with one warning.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.rules[*].limit
properties.description: The limit as `<count>/<duration>`: `5/1m`, `120/1m`, `10/s`.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.rules[*].methods
properties.description: The HTTP methods the rule is for; empty for all.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.rules[*].name
properties.description: The rule's name: part of its keys in the store, and what the logs call it. Default: `rule-<n>`, its place in the list from 1. Name a rule so that reordering the list does not start its buckets anew.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.rules[*].on-store-failure
properties.description: What happens to a request of this rule when the store cannot be reached; not set: `spring.web.rate-limit.on-store-failure`.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.rules[*].path
properties.description: The paths the rule is for, as a mapping's pattern (`/api/**`, `/api/users/{id}`), inside the context path.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.store
properties.description: Where the buckets are kept: `memory` (this isolate), `primary-isolate` (the first isolate, for all of a pool), `jdbc` (the primary `DataSource`, data starter), `procedure` (a database function, Supabase starter), or the name another library gives its store. Not set: the most specific the application has, in that order from the last. A `RateLimitStore` bean of the application wins over all.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.store-failure-retry-after
properties.description: The `Retry-After` of the 503 a request gets when the store cannot be reached and the failure denies.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.trusted-proxies
properties.description: The reverse proxies in front of the server: addresses and CIDR ranges (IPv4 and IPv6). Only a connection from one of them has its [clientAddressHeader] read, and the client is the entry the first trusted proxy added, counting from the right. Empty (the default): no header is ever read, the client is the connection's own address.

properties.name: spring.web.rate-limit.verify-store
properties.description: Whether the store is asked at startup that what it keeps its buckets in is there (the table or the function of its migration, its binding): the application does not start without it, and says what to run. A store that cannot be reached at that moment is a warning, not a failed start. `false` skips the check (and its one call to the store).

properties.name: trace
properties.description: Any value but `false` (for example `--trace`) sets the framework loggers to trace.
